package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript that, when executed, attempts to disable Windows Defender by invoking a PowerShell command. This is a direct attempt to weaken system security and is not a behavior expected from any legitimate npm package.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the package is executed or imported
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file (index.js or equivalent entry point)
required_permissions: administrative privileges (to modify Windows Defender settings)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code spawns a child process using child_process.exec to execute a PowerShell command that disables Windows Defender's real-time monitoring, resulting in reduced system defenses and increased risk of further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code attempts to disable Windows Defender's real-time protection, which is a well-known tactic used by malware to evade detection and facilitate further malicious activity. The use of obfuscation further indicates an attempt to hide malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not attempt to alter or disable system security settings, especially antivirus protections, nor should they execute privileged system commands without clear, user-initiated intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only specialized system administration or security management tools, typically run by IT administrators with explicit user consent, may disable Defender as part of a managed policy. General-purpose npm packages should never perform such actions automatically.
key_indicators: Presence of heavily obfuscated JavaScript code
Use of child_process.exec to run system-level commands
Direct attempt to disable Windows Defender real-time monitoring

attack_chain.action: User installs and executes the malicious package, triggering the obfuscated code in the main entry file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Windows Defender's real-time monitoring is disabled, significantly reducing system security and enabling further malicious activity or persistence.

behavioral_signatures: Heavily obfuscated JavaScript present in npm package files
Use of child_process or exec to invoke system-level commands
Execution of PowerShell commands that modify Windows Defender or other endpoint protection settings
Automatic disabling of antivirus protections without user consent
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing obfuscated code
References to 'Set-MpPreference' or 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring' in JavaScript or embedded PowerShell commands
Presence of child_process.exec calls with PowerShell command strings
network_indicators: None observed in this specific sample; no C2 or exfiltration activity detected in the analyzed code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated scanners should analyze npm packages for the presence of obfuscated JavaScript, especially in entry-point files. Flag any use of child_process or exec that invokes PowerShell commands related to Windows Defender or antivirus settings. Specifically, detect code that attempts to run 'Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true'. Any package exhibiting these behaviors should be considered highly suspicious and subject to further review.
